title: Introduction to Probability Theory I
description: The first probability course: counting techniques, axiomatic and conditional probability, the law of total probability and Bayes' rule, random variables and expectation, joint and marginal distributions, the Bernoulli, binomial and Poisson distributions, the normal distribution, and sampling distributions with point estimation. Built from the STA 115 lectures of Prof. O.I. Shittu, Dr A.U. Chukwu and Dr O.E. Olubusoye, with tests from 2016/17 to 2023 and STA 112 Probability I papers (the former code).

topics.title: Counting Techniques
topics.summary: Counting tells us how many outcomes an experiment has. The basic principle of counting, sampling with and without replacement, permutations (including identical and circular arrangements) and combinations are the tools used to work out probabilities.
subtopics: Circular arrangements and the binomial theorem

topics.title: Axiomatic and Conditional Probability
topics.summary: Probability is built on a sample space of outcomes and events. It satisfies three axioms, from which rules such as the complement and addition rules follow. Conditional probability and independence describe how one event changes the chance of another.
subtopics: Random experiments, sample spaces and events
Set theory: unions, intersections and De Morgan's laws
The three axioms and their consequences

topics.title: The Law of Total Probability and Bayes' Rule
topics.summary: When the sample space splits into mutually exclusive cases, the law of total probability builds P(E) from the conditional probabilities in each case. Bayes' rule turns these around to find the probability of a case given that E has happened.

topics.title: Random Variables, Expectation and Joint Distributions
topics.summary: A random variable assigns a number to each outcome. Discrete variables have probability mass functions and continuous ones have density functions. Expected value and variance summarise them, and joint and marginal distributions describe two variables together.
subtopics: Discrete pmfs and the distribution function F(x)
Moments, variance and the coefficient of variation
Joint, marginal and independent random variables

topics.title: Discrete Distributions: Bernoulli, Binomial and Poisson
topics.summary: The Bernoulli distribution models one trial with two outcomes, the binomial counts successes in n independent trials, and the Poisson counts random events in an interval. The hypergeometric distribution handles sampling without replacement.
subtopics: Bernoulli trials and the Bernoulli distribution
The Poisson distribution and its mean and variance

topics.title: The Normal Distribution
topics.summary: The normal distribution is the bell-shaped, symmetric distribution that models many measurements. Any normal variable is standardised with z = (x − µ)/σ, and probabilities come from the standard normal table.
subtopics: Shape and properties of the normal curve
The normal pdf and the notation N(µ, σ²)
The standard normal Z and z-tables
Probabilities between, above and below values
Finding a value from a probability

topics.title: Sampling Distributions and Point Estimation
topics.summary: A sampling distribution is the distribution of a statistic over all possible samples. The sample mean and sample proportion have known means and standard errors, which link samples to populations. Point and interval estimates use them to estimate parameters.
subtopics: Sampling distribution of the mean, with and without replacement
Sampling distribution of a proportion; sums and differences
